# Consent Form

**Protocol title:** Understanding the potential of LLMs for data discovery

**Study title:** Usefulness of Automatically Generated Genomics Visualizations

**Principal investigator:** Dr. Nils Gehlenborg

**Contact:** astrid_vandenbrandt@hms.harvard.edu

**Version date:** Jan 14, 2026

## Key Information

The following is a short summary of this study to help you decide whether or not to participate.

### Why am I being invited to take part in a research study?

We have invited you to take part in a research study because you have experience analyzing
and/or visualizing genomic or biomedical data as part of your work, training, or research
activities.

### What should I know about a research study?

* Whether or not you take part is up to you.
* You can choose not to take part.
* You can agree to take part and later change your mind.
* Your decision will not be held against you.
* You can ask all the questions you want before you decide.

### Why is this research being done?

Visualizations of genomic data are increasingly produced automatically by large language models
rather than written by hand. The purpose of this research is to learn how useful such
automatically generated visualizations are for researchers, and whether automated quality
scores agree with the judgement of people who work with this kind of data.

### How long will I take part in this research?

We expect that you will be in this research for about 65 minutes, during which you will
complete a single online session.

### What will I be asked to do?

If you agree to participate, you will first answer a few questions about your background. After
a short set of instructions and several practice items with feedback,
you will rate 15 visualizations one at a time. For each one, you are shown the
request a researcher made, a preview of the input data, and a live interactive rendering, and
rate how useful the visualization is on a scale from 1 to 5. Where a rating is 3 or below, a
short follow-up asks which aspects were wrong.

### Is there any way being in this study could be bad for me?

The risks associated with this study are minimal. Some participants may experience mild
discomfort, boredom or difficulty while answering questions or rating the visualizations. There
is also a minimal risk of breach of confidentiality, which will be mitigated through data
security and privacy protections.

### Will being in this study help me in any way?

There are no direct benefits to you from participating in this research; however, the findings
may help improve data visualization methods and AI-assisted tools for future users.

### Will I be paid to participate in this research?

You will receive a $50 Amazon gift card upon completion of the study.

### Will I have to pay for anything to participate in this research?

It will not cost you anything to participate in this research.

### What happens if I do not want to be in this research?

Participation in research is voluntary. You can decide to participate, not to participate, or
stop participation at any time without penalty or loss of benefits to which you are otherwise
entitled. Your alternative to participating in this research study is not to participate.

## Statement of Consent

I have read the information in this consent form including risks and possible benefits. All my
questions about the research have been answered to my satisfaction. I understand that I am free
to withdraw at any time without penalty or loss of benefits to which I am otherwise entitled.
